subject: Support packaging: uptime tiers, on-call escalation & credit caps
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Verma <samir@acme.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Options for SLA & premium support — quick clarity needed

Hi Samir,

Thanks again for the time yesterday. To move the pricing conversation forward I wanted to clarify a couple of points so that procurement and I can put together a neat options matrix for you:

- Desired uptime target (we offer 99.5%, 99.9%, 99.95% as standard tiers)
- Preferred incident response times (business-hours vs 24x7 on-call escalation)
- Credit caps you’re comfortable with if an SLA is missed (standard is % of monthly committed spend, can be capped)
- Any requirement for dedicated account engineering / named on-call vs shared pager coverage

If you can call out the target uptime and whether you need 24x7 escalation, I’ll circulate three pricing packages (Standard, Premium, Enterprise) with suggested discount bands for annual and multi-year commitments.

I’ve attached a short SLA_Tier_Comparison.pdf so you have the baseline language.

Best,
Sean
Sean Gallagher
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
(415) 555-0142

Attachment: SLA_Tier_Comparison.pdf (PDF, 134 KB)
From: Samir Verma <samir@acme.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Mar 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Options for SLA & premium support — quick clarity needed

Sean,

Thanks — a couple quick answers:
- We’re aiming for 99.9% (target for production workloads).
- Want 24x7 escalation to a named on-call engineer for P1s (we have a global ops team and need immediate handoff).
- For credits, we’re generally looking for a clear cap and prefer it not to exceed 50% of monthly committed spend for repeated misses; willing to discuss higher caps for higher uptime.
- Also: any room for a one-time onboarding credit if we sign a 2-year deal? Procurement is looking at TCO.

Can you send specific pricing options? I’ll loop procurement if needed.

—Samir
Samir Verma
Director, Site Reliability | Acme Corp
samir@acme.com

Subject: Fwd: Options for SLA & premium support — Acme specifics (99.9%, 24x7, credit cap ask)

Team — forwarding Samir’s responses. Need a quick alignment so I can send formal options back to Acme:

1) Confirm commercial levers: recommended discount bands for 2-year commit, and whether we can offer a one-time onboarding credit (how much and rules).
2) Legal: example language for credit caps (Samir suggested 50% monthly cap; they prefer not higher unless uptime >= 99.95%). Do we have precedent with Enterprise customers?
3) SE: estimate of named on-call (price and response SLA) — is this a premium add-on or part of our Enterprise plan?

I’d like to reply to Samir by end of day Monday with three clean options (Standard/Premium/Enterprise) and a neat explanation of escalation coverage and credit treatment.

Thanks —
Sean

> Attachment: Acme_MutualActionPlan.xlsx mentioned by Samir as potential follow-up
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 21 Mar 2026 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Fwd: Options for SLA & premium support — Acme specifics (99.9%, 24x7, credit cap ask)

Sean / team,

Draft pricing options below — these are intentionally distinct to give Acme negotiation room. All monthly prices assume a 1-node equivalent baseline; final pricing will scale to their committed capacity.

1) Standard (99.5%) — $8,500/mo
   - Business-hours support (M-F 9-5)
   - SLA credit: up to 25% of monthly committed spend per incident, cap 50% for repeated misses
   - No named on-call, shared escalation pool

2) Premium (99.9%) — $14,000/mo
   - 24x7 escalation to shared on-call with guaranteed initial response (30 min for P1)
   - SLA credit: up to 50% monthly committed spend per month (cap 75% cumulative over quarter if repeated)
   - One-time onboarding credit: up to $10,000 for 2-year commit

3) Enterprise (99.95%) — custom pricing (recommended starting at $25,000/mo)
   - 24x7 escalation to named on-call engineer + direct engineering pager (SLA: 15 min to acknowledge, 60 min remediation plan)
   - SLA credit: uncapped per incident but capped at 100% of monthly committed spend if there’s a systemic issue; separate remediation playbook and service credits plus product-level root cause analysis
   - Onboarding credit: negotiable (up to $25k for multi-year deals)

Negotiation levers: multi-year commit (10–20% discount), prepayment (additional 5–8%), cap on credits in exchange for higher monthly price, and defined remediation responsibilities for non-software causes.

Legal note (Laura) — I’ve flagged the credit language as likely to be the sticking point. We should avoid open-ended caps in public-facing SOWs. Laura, can you propose redlines that preserve our liability while offering Acme a clear recovery path?

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Director, Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai
From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Verma <samir@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2026 11:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Options for SLA & premium support — quick clarity needed

Hi Samir — appreciate the clarity. Based on your ask (99.9%, 24x7 named escalation for P1, desire for onboarding credit) we recommend the following two commercial paths — pick whichever best fits procurement:

Option A — Premium (straightforward)
- 99.9% uptime, 24x7 escalation to shared on-call (30 min initial response for P1), credit cap: 50% monthly committed spend, onboarding credit: $10k for 2-year sign
- Monthly: $14,000 (list) — available at 15% discount for signed 2-year commitment

Option B — Enterprise-lite (named on-call)
- 99.9% uptime, named on-call engineer with 30 min acknowledgement and 90 min remediation plan for P1, credit cap: 75% monthly committed spend, onboarding credit: $15k for 2-year sign
- Monthly: $18,500 (list) — available at 18% discount for 2-year commit

Notes / ask from Acme:
- If you need the credit cap lower than the values above we’ll need to move to higher uptime (99.95%) or take other commercial levers (multi-year prepay).
- We will draft SOW language that caps liability and ties credits to confirmed platform outages (not customer-side network or misconfiguration). Laura will propose the legal language.

I’ve attached the SLA_Tier_Comparison and a short Mutual Action Plan with timelines. If you’re aligned with either option I’ll generate an MPA + preliminary SOW and pull in Legal for redlines.

Best,
Sean

Attachment: Acme_MutualActionPlan.xlsx (Excel, 22 KB)
From: Samir Verma <samir@acme.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: Acme Procurement <procurement@acme.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2026 15:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Options for SLA & premium support — quick clarity needed

Sean,

Thanks — Option B (Enterprise-lite) is closest to what we need for our global production workload. A couple follow-ups before we proceed to MPA/DocuSign:

1) Can we get a 20% discount off the list monthly (so $14,800/mo) if we sign a 24-month deal with quarterly usage true-ups?
2) Can you confirm the cumulative credit cap treatment for repeated misses — we’d like the cap to be at least 100% monthly committed spend over a rolling 3-month window (not to exceed the total committed spend), otherwise the economics risk being unfavorable for us.
3) DocuSign / procurement path: please send the MPA + SOW draft and we’ll route through our procurement team.

If you can confirm those two items, we’re prepared to move quickly.

—Samir
Samir Verma
Director, Site Reliability | Acme Corp
procurement@acme.com
